title: BENDING STRESS ENHANCEMENT IN MATERIALS WITH LIMITED SHEAR RESISTANCE-PART I. SLIPPING-LAYERS MODEL
prior_art_family: discrete slipping layers / interface-resolved layered beam mechanics
scientific_question: How do progressive frictional slip zones across interfaces and unconstrained beam overhangs alter bending stresses and central deflections in discrete multi-layer beams?
reason_investigated: Foundational discrete-layer benchmark for Part II continuum theory; primary formulation of frictionally coupled slipping beams.
system_description: 16-layer discrete elastic beam with frictional interfaces in 3-point bending with overhang D.
material_description: Isotropic linear elastic layers with modulus E, coupled by frictional interfaces with shear strength tau_p.
geometry: Span L, total depth H, width b, layer count n = 16, individual layer thickness h = H/n, overhang D.
loading_mode: Quasi-static monotonic 3-point bending (central line load P).
boundary_conditions: Simply supported at x = +/- L/2 with overhang extending to x = +/- (L/2 + D).
control_variable: Normalized load p = P / P_s8, where P_s8 = 4*b*H*tau_p/3 is initial central slip load.
pressure_or_preload_definition: Uncoupled from normal stress; constant shear threshold tau_p on all interfaces.
mechanical_model: Discrete slipping-layers beam theory enforcing Bernoulli hypothesis per layer, equilibrium of beamlets, and Powell's optimization for slip zone boundaries.
constitutive_assumptions: Linear elastic layers; generalized Bernoulli hypothesis (plane sections per layer remain plane); zero opening/delamination.
contact_assumptions: Continuous interface contact; normal separation prohibited; shear traction cannot exceed tau_p.
friction_assumptions: Rigid-plastic shear slip criterion: tau = tau_p * sgn(Delta u) during sliding, |tau| <= tau_p during stick; pressure-independent threshold.
slip_representation: Explicit interface displacement jumps Delta u_i(x) with internal slip zones of half-length R_i; stick outside R_i.
stiffness_definition: Secant bending stiffness derived from central load-deflection P vs w(0); bounded between fully bonded EI_solid and completely slipping n*EI_layer.
measured_observables: Maximum axial stress ratio S_i,max / sigma_max
global_observables: Slip initiation load ratios P_si / P_s8
model_validation_method: Self-consistent numerical convergence using Powell's optimization; no physical experiments.
main_evidence: Demonstrates that discrete interface slip initiates on the central interface at P_s8 and propagates outward, magnifying outer fiber stresses up to 4x equivalent solid beam stress.
what_it_proves: Discrete interface slip significantly alters normal stress distribution, causing individual layers to bend locally.
Beam overhang D carries non-zero layer moments/forces that stiffen the structure against midspan deflection.
Provides a high-fidelity interface-resolved reference for multi-layer slipping beams.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not validate a homogenized continuum model.
Does not incorporate vacuum-induced normal confinement or Coulomb pressure-dependent friction.
Does not provide physical experimental validation or error tolerance limits.
limitations: Computationally intensive discrete formulation limited to simple monotonic loading.
Decoupled from transverse normal stress (constant tau_p rather than mu * sigma_n).
No experimental testing; monotonic small-deformation assumption.
threat_to_D1_claims: Foundational discrete reference. Proves that multi-layer slipping beams exhibit complex local stress redistribution that continuum models struggle to capture.
supports_D1_claims: Supports D1's premise that discrete layer mechanics have distinct localized phenomena (stress magnification, discrete slip fronts) requiring rigorous validity bounds.
conceptual_overlap: High on multi-layer beam slip mechanics; zero on vacuum pressure regulation.
mechanistic_overlap: Frictional interlayer slip with individual layer bending; lacks Coulomb normal pressure coupling.
model_overlap: High with discrete-layer baseline; complementary to homogenized continuum models.
breakdown_assessment: Slip-initiation loads P_si are physical regime transitions, not model breakdown boundaries.
model_form_error_assessment: Discrete reference model; does not evaluate continuum model-form error.
failure_mechanism_analysis: Interfacial shear yield followed by excessive deflection and local tensile stress magnification.
impact_on_D1: Provides primary discrete reference used to audit Steif Part II (f00d886124). Bounded to constant shear threshold without vacuum confinement.
homogenization_assumptions: None. Each layer is treated as an individual Bernoulli beam with separate displacement fields.
moment_curvature_relationship: Piecewise linear/nonlinear moment-curvature governed by sequential slip-zone expansion across 15 internal interfaces.
jamming_or_slipping_regimes: Four stages: Stage I (stick), Stage II (central interface slipping), Stage III (intermediate interfaces slipping), Stage IV (all interfaces slipping).
yield_or_slip_criteria: Tresca-like constant shear traction yield criterion: |tau| = tau_p.
energy_or_dissipation_treatment: Frictional energy dissipation integrated across discrete slipping interfaces W_f = sum int tau_p * |Delta u_i| dx.

micro_to_macro_mapping.micro_inputs: 16 individual layer Young's moduli E, layer thickness h, interface shear strength tau_p.
micro_to_macro_mapping.mapping_assumptions: Kinematic compatibility of transverse deflection w(x) across all layers; continuity of shear traction.
micro_to_macro_mapping.macro_outputs: Gross beam deflection w(x), effective flexural rigidity, peak axial stress.
micro_to_macro_mapping.validation_evidence: Numerical convergence; self-consistent equilibrium across beamlet subdivisions.

breakdown_mechanism: Computational intractability for general distributed loads or high layer counts; failure when shear slip reaches specimen ends.
systematic_residuals_nature: None reported (serves as exact discrete reference).

claim_linkage_details.effect_type: Establishes discrete multi-layer frictional slipping baseline.
Shows discrete layer models require extensive computational resources, motivating homogenized models.

w05_cross_reference.notes: Not analyzed in W05. Acts as discrete benchmark for Steif Part II.

title: Bending Stress Enhancement in Materials with Limited Shear Resistance-Part II. Unlayered Shear-Weak Model
prior_art_family: homogenized continuum / unlayered shear-weak beam mechanics
scientific_question: Can an unlayered shear-weak continuum model accurately reproduce the deflection and stress enhancement of discrete multi-layer slipping beams as n -> infinity?
reason_investigated: Closest historical predecessor to homogenized continuum modeling of layered slipping beams; evaluates asymptotic convergence and finite-n error.
system_description: Unlayered continuous beam with elastic bending and elastic-perfectly plastic shear core representing n -> infinity slipping layers.
material_description: Homogenized material with longitudinal Young's modulus E and limiting shear yield strength tau_p.
geometry: Span L, total depth H, width b, aspect ratio L/H = 5, overhang ratio D/L.
loading_mode: Quasi-static monotonic 3-point bending with central load P.
control_variable: Applied shear force V or dimensionless load P / (b * H * tau_p).
pressure_or_preload_definition: Uncoupled from normal stress; constant shear yield stress tau_p.
mechanical_model: Unlayered shear-weak beam theory: Timoshenko-like kinematics where transverse shear stress distribution yields plastically when reaching tau_p, creating an internal plastic shear zone.
constitutive_assumptions: Elastic axial stress sigma_x = E * epsilon_x; elastic-perfectly plastic shear response with yield stress tau_p.
contact_assumptions: Discrete interfaces smeared into continuous shear strain field gamma(x, y).
friction_assumptions: Smeared plastic shear yielding represents interfacial Coulomb friction under constant normal confinement.
slip_representation: Plastic shear strain gamma^p(x, y) across cross section; discrete slip jumps are fully homogenized.
stiffness_definition: Tangent and secant bending-shear compliance derived from elastic core height and plastic zone extent.
measured_observables: Relative errors e1 and e2 against Part I
experimental_method: None. Pure analytical derivation and numerical benchmarking.
model_validation_method: Quantitative benchmarking against Part I 16-layer discrete model and exact n -> infinity limit.
validation_parameters: Errors e1 and e2 defined against Part I 16-layer calculations
main_evidence: Shows that unlayered continuum model matches finite-n discrete model with error e1 < 5% across intermediate loads, but breaks down catastrophically as shear force approaches continuum load ceiling V_max = b*H*tau_p.
what_it_proves: Asymptotic convergence of discrete slipping-layer mechanics to an unlayered shear-weak continuum as n -> infinity.
Homogenized models can accurately predict midspan deflection and plastic zone size for moderate loads.
Defines quantitative error metrics e1 and e2 comparing continuum to discrete predictions.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not declare an acceptable error tolerance a priori (Option A satisfied, Option B not satisfied).
Does not map a tolerance-defined validity domain across layer count n and normal pressure.
Does not account for pressure-dependent friction or vacuum envelope confinement.
limitations: Cannot support shear forces above V_max = b*H*tau_p, whereas physical finite-n beams carry higher shear via individual layer bending.
Underpredicts peak local bending stresses by ignoring individual layer curvature.
No experimental validation.
threat_to_D1_claims: High conceptual threat to claims of novelty in continuum modeling of slipping layers. Demonstrates that homogenization of slipping layers was achieved in 1993.
supports_D1_claims: Directly supports D1's core thesis: homogenized slip models possess severe model-form error and breakdown near load/shear ceilings, proving the need for validity limit mapping.
conceptual_overlap: Very high on continuum homogenization of slipping layers; zero on vacuum pressure control.
mechanistic_overlap: Plastic shear yielding representing smeared slip; lacks pressure-dependent friction coupling.
model_overlap: Direct predecessor to homogenized layer-jamming beam models.
breakdown_assessment: MODEL BREAKDOWN STUDIED: Identifies divergence between continuum and discrete models near V_max where discrete beam continues to carry load through layer bending moments while continuum reaches yield plateau.
model_form_error_assessment: Quantifies model-form error via e1 (shear force discrepancy at fixed slip length) and e2 (slip length discrepancy at fixed shear force); error grows sharply near V_max.
failure_mechanism_analysis: Continuum shear-capacity exhaustion (V -> V_max) causing unphysical unbounded curvature in continuum theory.
impact_on_D1: Critical prior art. Establishes mathematical homogenization of slipping layers, but fails to execute D1's scientific act (predeclared tolerance, pressure-dependence, experimental validation).
homogenization_assumptions: Discrete layer count n -> infinity; interfacial slip displacement jumps smeared into continuous plastic shear strain field gamma^p(y).
rve_or_average_field_definition: Continuous cross-section through beam depth H; shear stress tau(y) distributed parabolically in elastic core and truncated at tau_p in yielded outer zones.
moment_curvature_relationship: Nonlinear moment-curvature relation M(kappa) coupled with transverse shear resultant V; exhibits reduced flexural stiffness once plastic shear zones initiate.
jamming_or_slipping_regimes: Elastic unyielded regime (V < 2*b*H*tau_p/3), progressive core yielding regime, and limiting shear capacity regime (V -> b*H*tau_p).
yield_or_slip_criteria: Smeared Tresca-like shear yield criterion |tau(y)| = tau_p.
energy_or_dissipation_treatment: Plastic dissipation energy rate D = int tau_p * |dot{gamma}^p| dA.

micro_to_macro_mapping.micro_inputs: Discrete layer interfaces with constant shear threshold tau_p and layer thickness h.
micro_to_macro_mapping.mapping_assumptions: Continuous limit n -> infinity; neglected individual layer flexural rigidity (E*h^3/12 -> 0).
micro_to_macro_mapping.macro_outputs: Homogenized shear-weak Timoshenko-like beam governing equations.
micro_to_macro_mapping.lost_micro_information: Individual layer bending stiffness, discrete slip-front steps, localized layer boundary liftoff.
micro_to_macro_mapping.validation_evidence: Quantitative comparison with Part I 16-layer discrete model using error measures e1 and e2.

calibration_vs_validation_separation.validation_data: Part I discrete numerical results for n=16.
calibration_vs_validation_separation.shared_vs_independent_data: Part I is an independent discrete mechanical formulation.

breakdown_mechanism: Continuum reaches plastic shear limit V_max where effective shear compliance diverges, whereas finite-n discrete beam retains residual stiffness via layer bending.
systematic_residuals_nature: Continuum model underestimates beam shear carrying capacity near V_max and underestimates peak local fiber stress by omitting layer-level bending.

claim_linkage_details.effect_type: Proves unlayered continuum models for slipping layers exist since 1993.
Provides historical precedent for model breakdown near load limits, confirming necessity of validity boundaries.
Demonstrates Option A (asymptotic comparison) was done in 1993, requiring D1 to deliver Option B (predeclared tolerance-defined boundary).

w05_cross_reference.notes: Not included in W05 (W05 was restricted to direct layer jamming). Forms core continuum baseline for W06.
